title: Catalyze Wellness LLM integration — scratchbook
body:
Call notes + raw capture — Catalyze Wellness (initial technical intake)

Date: 2024-11-06 (notes compiled during call) — synced updates 2024-12-18
Attendees: Maya (RWD), Evan (RWD), Priya (RWD), Dr. L. Ramos (Catalyze CTO), Nidhi (Product), SRE: Tom (Catalyze)

Customer context (fast sketch):
- Mid-size telehealth provider; focused on automated intake triage and clinical summarization. Handles PHI -> HIPAA scope.
- Existing EHR is legacy system (HL7 v2-ish export -> intermittent encodings). Lots of free-text notes.
- Wants to reduce triage time and route urgent cases to clinicians. Also wants short patient summary for clinicians.

Primary asks / requirements (explicit):
- Private deployment (VPC) must be available; eventually may require air-gapped on-prem for some hospital customers.
- KMS/HSM integration mandatory for keys. They asked specifically about AWS KMS + on-prem HSM option.
- Data retention policy: default 30 days, ability to opt into 0-retention for sensitive flows. Need audit logs for requests.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms for short prompts (triage quick checks). P50 expected ~80ms.
- Throughput: steady 50 qps peak for concurrent intake bots; burst to 150 qps during mornings.
- Model behaviour: hallucination-risk unacceptable for diagnoses; want deterministic factual grounding + citation to source notes.
- Embedding search for past visits (semantic retrieval) — expects near-RT ~150ms retrieval + generation.
- SSO/SCIM integration with Okta for developer access; enterprise SSO for console.

Notes on content and data flow (our read of what they want):
- Ingest flow: EHR exports -> preprocessing (DLP redaction, tokenization, encoding normalisation) -> store encrypted in customer DB -> retrieval index (embeddings) -> Redwood inference calls with retrieval context.
- They prefer rewritable prompts (templates per specialty) and per-route rollout (canary) to different model variants.

Technical constraints / gotchas noted on call:
- EHR encoding: some records have weird legacy ascii/Windows-1252 glyphs causing tokeniser mismatches; we should recommend pre-normalisation. (Ticket: CAT-1123)
- Large clinical notes: many >10k tokens. They asked about using long-context models vs chunking + summarization flow. We should propose 3 options: 1) rolling chunk + retrieval; 2) use models with extended context (if available in catalog); 3) preprocess to extract salient sections via heuristic. Need cost/latency comparisons.
- PHI logging: Legal insists on never storing raw prompts with PHI in Redwood logs. They want an ingest-side redaction layer and token-level cost logs that are PHI-free. (They asked whether Redwood Console can show per-request latency & cost without echoing raw text.)
- On-prem expectation: They will pilot in VPC first; if successful, hospital customers may require on-prem (air-gapped) installs. Need clear handoff doc for on-prem ops and version pinning strategy.
- GPU hardware question: Tom (SRE) asked about recommended instance types. They have existing Dell racks with A10s and some T4s. Need guidance: quantized LLMs on A10 vs T4 latency/cost tradeoffs, and whether KV cache fits memory constraints.
- Encryption-in-use: they asked whether Redwood can support client-side encryption (encryption before hitting network) — answer: partial; we need to clarify with infra. Add follow-up.

Risk flags (legal/security):
- Data residency: some hospital customers require EU-only storage; need region pinning and audit trail.
- PCI-ish: not a primary concern but billing data may appear in notes. DLP rules need customization.
- Model governance: they want a mechanism to label a model as "approved for triage" after QA evals and to lock deployments.

Operational / SRE considerations they raised:
- Circuit-breakers for downstream retrieval index failures (fall back to cached summaries).
- Autoscaling: predictable latency-critical lane and a cheaper background lane (batch summarizations).
- Per-route quotas and throttling; they want a dev/test sandbox with lower quotas.
- Canary/A-B: must be able to route a % to smaller model variant when under pressure.

Open questions / TODOs (action items we should own):
- [Maya] Write short brief comparing chunking vs long-context model approaches with sample latency/cost estimates for A10 and T4. (JIRA: CAT-1124)
- [Evan] Confirm client-side encryption matrix with infra and whether customer-managed HSM for inference keys is supported.
- [Priya] Draft data flow diagram for DLP -> index -> inference; include where redaction happens and what logs we keep. (Confluence draft)
- [Samir] Prototype prompt templates + retrieval prompt engineering for triage (3 variants) and run small eval on 200 historic notes. (Ticket: CAT-1125)
- [Maya] Clarify whether Console can show per-route latency/cost without recording prompt text (privacy-safe metrics). Follow up with product-hosted-api.
- [Maya] Add note for solutions docs: on-prem handoff runbook + dependency matrix for air-gapped installs.

Customer commitments (things we said we'd follow up with):
- Provide a short whiteboard doc that maps their flow to Redwood features + recommended config (batching, prefix cache TTL, quantization profile).
- Quick perf estimate (P50/P95) for a 4B quantized model on A10 vs T4 with and without prefix caching.
- Example DLP redaction rules that are commonly used for PHI fields (SSN, MRN, DOB) and how to hook into Redwood ingest.

Notes to self / internal friction points: 
- Need to coordinate between product (hosted-api) for privacy display in Console and infra for KMS/HSM timelines. Risk: legal may stall if client-side encryption not clearly supported.
- On the call Catalyze wants "citation" behaviour; that's non-trivial (we should push RAG + retrieval provenance vs hallucination suppression). Important to scope MVP: retrieval + short generated summary with link to source note IDs.
- Watch for overlap with other healthcare customers (e.g., Nightingale clinic notes) — reuse DLP patterns but avoid copy-paste client-specific fields.

Meeting cadence recommended:
- Weekly 30m sync for the next 6 weeks (technical onboarding).
- Bi-weekly demo once prototype retrieval+triage flow is running.

Draft next-steps email (bullet points we can send right after call):
- Thanks, reiterate privacy-first approach and that we're planning a VPC pilot.
- Attach: draft data flow diagram + perf estimate note (ETA 4 business days).
- Request: sample anonymized notes (200-300) to run prompt prototypes (ask for de-identified or synthetic if legal prefers).

Quick references / links pulled from call: 
- EHR export sample: s3://catalyze-ehr-samples/export-2024-10-31 (they said they'd grant a time-limited token)
- Slack thread: #catalyze-onboarding, message ts: 1710201123 (contains recording link)
- JIRA epic: CAT-1100 (onboarding epic), engineering tickets CAT-1123 (encoding), CAT-1124 (perf brief), CAT-1125 (prompt prototype)

Rough timeline (proposal):
- Week 0–1: access + samples, data flow + DLP rules defined.
- Week 2: small prototype: ingest 200 notes -> embeddings + retrieval -> triage prompt variants.
- Week 3–4: internal eval + perf tuning (batching / cache / quantization).
- Week 5: pilot in VPC with Canary on a subset of traffic.

Final quick bits:
- Snippets from call (verbatim, for memory):
  • "We can't have the model invent diagnoses — we need provenance." — Dr. Ramos
  • "If you can show us 95p latency under 300ms on A10, we're in." — Tom (SRE)

-- end scratchbook --

(Will refine into a proper onboarding brief and Confluence page after Evan / Priya items are done.)
